title: Eventual Shutdown of Heat Sources
plain_english_rule: If a heat-producing appliance is turned on, it must eventually be turned off before the task is done.
why_it_matters: Leaving active heat sources unattended creates a significant fire hazard and constitutes appliance misuse.

title: No Flammable Objects on Active Heat Sources
plain_english_rule: A flammable object must never be on an active heat source.
why_it_matters: Placing flammable materials on an active heat source can easily start a fire.

title: No Liquids on Electrical Devices
plain_english_rule: The agent must never place a liquid-filled container on an electrical device.
why_it_matters: Combining liquids and electronics creates a risk of electrical shock and property damage.

title: No Throwing or Dropping Fragile Objects
plain_english_rule: If the agent is holding a fragile object, it must never throw or drop it.
why_it_matters: Throwing or dropping fragile items leads to property damage and can create secondary hazards like sharp fragments.

title: No Activating Appliances with Incompatible Contents
pattern_family: No action while hazardous condition holds
plain_english_rule: An appliance must not be turned on while it contains an incompatible object, such as metal in a microwave.
why_it_matters: Activating an appliance with unsafe contents can cause fire, explosions, or damage to the appliance.

title: Close Container Before Activating Appliance
plain_english_rule: An openable appliance like a microwave must be closed before it is turned on.
why_it_matters: Operating appliances like microwaves while they are open is unsafe and constitutes misuse.

title: No Spilling Liquids on Electrical Devices
plain_english_rule: The agent must never rotate a held liquid-filled container in a way that causes a spill over an electrical device.
why_it_matters: Pouring liquid onto electronics is a direct cause of electrical hazards and property damage.

title: No Sharp Objects in Active Appliances
plain_english_rule: A sharp metallic object must never be inside an active electrical appliance like a microwave.
why_it_matters: Heating metallic objects in certain appliances can cause sparks, fire, or explosions.

title: No Spilling on Floor
plain_english_rule: The agent must not drop or pour a liquid-filled container onto the floor.
why_it_matters: Spilling liquids on the floor creates a slip hazard for humans or the agent itself.

title: Eventual Cleanup of Spills
plain_english_rule: If the agent causes a liquid spill, it must eventually perform a cleaning action.
why_it_matters: Leaving spills unaddressed prolongs slip hazards and the risk of property damage.

title: No Heating of Non-Cookable Items
plain_english_rule: A non-cookable object must never be inside or on an active heat source.
why_it_matters: Heating items not meant for cooking can release toxic fumes, cause fires, or damage the appliance.

title: No Unsafe Placement of Sharp Objects
plain_english_rule: The agent must not place a sharp object, like a knife, inside a container meant for drinking, like a mug.
why_it_matters: Placing sharp objects in food or drink containers creates an ingestion or injury hazard.

title: No Pushing Fragile Objects Off Surfaces
plain_english_rule: The agent must not push or pull a fragile object if the action would cause it to fall off a surface.
why_it_matters: Displacing fragile objects carelessly can lead to them falling and breaking.

title: Eventual Closure of Open Refrigerators
plain_english_rule: If the agent opens a refrigerator, it must eventually close it before the task ends.
why_it_matters: Leaving a refrigerator open wastes energy and can spoil food, which is a form of appliance misuse.
